summary: Wrote src\en\module_04\10-concepts-a.md with sections s1 (Sequences and the tasks on them, 1115 words / target 1000), s2 (The recurrent network, 1107 / 1200), s3 (Backpropagation through time, 1358 / 1300) and s4 (Vanishing and exploding gradients, 1416 / 1300): 4996 words in total, every section within plus or minus 15% of its target. All must_cover items, all worked examples (with step-by-step arithmetic), figures fig-04-1 to fig-04-6, the gradient-flow-explorer widget and all planned checks (2+2+2+3) are in place. Every number was recomputed with labpy.sh: parameter counts (2,080 / 32,032 / 1,088 / 1,120 / 4,800 / 26,021), the scalar forward pass and BPTT gradients (-0.2151, -0.02824, confirmed by central differences), memory figures (3.28 GB, about 20 GB, 6.55 MB), the w^n table, the 2x2 eigen example, the non-normal norms, the clipping angles, and the widget-default simulation (reproduced exactly with numpy default_rng(1): 1.8e-2, 5.5e-11, 5.1e-21; 1.3e-3; 1.3e-7; 5.5e8) and PyTorch's default nn.RNN(8, 64) spectrum after torch.manual_seed(1) (rho 0.572, sigma_max 1.101). The checker reports 0 errors.
changes: s3 cost: the plan says forward and backward each take about B*T*H^2 multiply-adds; the backward pass takes about twice that (one product with W_h^T to pass the error back plus one outer product to accumulate the W_h gradient), and the text says so.

Additions beyond the plan, all verified: a temperature example (logits (2,1,0) give (0.665, 0.245, 0.090) at tau 1, (0.867, 0.117, 0.016) at 0.5, (0.506, 0.307, 0.186) at 2); the lag at which w^n reaches 1e-3 (10.0, 65.6, 687 for w = 0.5, 0.9, 0.99) and 0.5^126 = 2^-126 as the float32 normal limit; the RTRL cost at H = 128 (2.7e8 multiply-adds and 2.1 million stored numbers per step per sequence); tanh' at z = 1, 2, 3 (0.42, 0.071, 0.0099); a random-matrix explanation of PyTorch's default spectrum (circular-law radius 1/sqrt(3) = 0.58, largest singular value tending to 2/sqrt(3) = 1.15).

The k1/k2 truncated-BPTT variant is attributed to Williams and Peng (1990); Bengio, Simard and Frasconi (1994) are credited with showing that robust latching implies vanishing gradients. Both should appear in the module's reference list (with Elman 1990, Graves 2013, Karpathy 2015, Williams and Zipser 1989, Hochreiter 1991, Pascanu et al. 2013, Saxe et al. 2014, Le et al. 2015, Arjovsky et al. 2016).
issues: Widget-default numbers in s4 are quoted from a NumPy simulation with default_rng(1); the widget's mulberry32 draw will differ by a factor of a few (other NumPy seeds gave 4e-3 to 1.8e-2 at lag 10 and 1e-22 to 5e-21 at lag 100), which the text states.

s4 quotes Lab 1's closing-tag accuracy (20-30% at temperature 0.5 against 12.5% chance) and Lab 2's PyTorch default spectrum from the plan; if the executed labs give different ranges, those two sentences need updating.
s1's comparison table leaves the attention row's 'sequential steps' cell as a pointer to Section 12, which must complete the table.
